papers.titleEn: Covalent Organic Framework-Templated Spatial Confinement of Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as efficient hole-contacting layers for p-i-n perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, incomplete SAM coverage and weak bonding with the substrate result in heterogeneous buried interfaces. Herein, a covalent organic framework (COF)-templated spatial confinement (CTSC) strategy is developed by employing a newly designed phosphonate-carbazole-based COF, namely COF-TPACz, to regulate the buried interface. The nanoscale island-like COF domains could restrict the penetration of aggregated SAM molecules and allow well-distributed ones to anchor on exposed substrates. Meanwhile, hydrogen-bonding and π-π interactions between COF-TPACz and SAM favor a more uniform molecular arrangement on the COF domains. These adjustments synergistically suppress molecular aggregation and improve surface coverage, yielding a denser and more homogeneous SAM interface. Furthermore, the improved interface optimizes upper perovskite crystallization, promotes compact and vertically extended grains, and strengthens buried interfacial contact, thereby suppressing nonradiative recombination and facilitating charge extraction and transport. Consequently, the CTSC-based PSCs achieve a peak efficiency of 27.03%, together with enhanced long-term stability. We believe these findings provide a conceptual advance for realizing homogeneous SAM via spatial confinement and a viable route toward efficient and stable PSCs.
papers.filename: Jianyu Yuan, Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2026, Covalent Organic Framework-Templated Spatial Confinement of Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Perovskite Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Electrochemical sensor array for assessment of oxidative stress in canine urine
papers.abstract: Heatstroke (HS) in working dogs is a severe clinical condition characterized by high mortality, rapid onset, and grave physiological damage largely driven by excessive oxidative stress (OS), which is caused by an imbalance between antioxidants and reactive oxygen species. Accurate and rapid quantification of oxidative biomarkers, including total antioxidant capacity (TAC), total oxidant status (TOS), and the OS index (OSI), is essential for timely diagnosis and intervention. However, current diagnostic approaches are invasive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for field applications. In this study, we present a novel electrochemical electronic tongue (e-tongue) sensor for OS assessment based upon canine urine samples. The device consists of a microfabricated chip with eleven working electrodes, comprising bare gold electrodes and electrodes modified with nanomaterials (molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ), reduced graphene oxide (rGO), and platinum black (PtB)), that generates partially selective electrochemical signals from the various antioxidants and reactive oxygen species in the urine samples. The set of cross-reactive electrochemical signals was recorded using differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) and then examined with chemometric models principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares regression (PLSR) to predict the OS levels. Validation against reference colorimetric assays demonstrated promising performance, with correlation coefficients of 0.785, 0.745, and 0.764 and root mean square errors of 7.21 μM, 0.016 mM, and 0.628 for TAC, TOS, and OSI, respectively. This work exhibits the first published application of an electrochemical e-tongue for OS monitoring in veterinary medicine, showcasing a portable, and field-deployable solution for real-time canine biomarker assessment.
papers.filename: Hadar Ben‐Yoav, Sens. Actuators B Chem., 2026, Electrochemical sensor array for assessment of oxidative stress in canine urine

papers.titleEn: High-Performance Lead and Lead-Free Inverted Perovskite Photodiodes: From Self-Powered Optical Sensing to X-Ray Detection
papers.abstract: The performance gap between n‐i‐p and p‐i‐n metal halide perovskite photodiodes remains poorly understood. This study compares triple‐cation photodiodes, demonstrating that a p‐i‐n stack utilizing MeO‐2PACz monolayers and C 60 /BCP transport layers achieves superior self‐powered performance. The p‐i‐n configuration yields a zero‐bias Linear Dynamic Range of 135–146 dB (638–450 nm illumination), a cut‐off frequency of ∼9 kHz, and suppresses flicker noise to achieve a specific detectivity ( D* ) exceeding 10 14 Jones. Conversely, the n‐i‐p stack suffers from higher dark current, severe hysteresis, and interfacial charge accumulation. Impedance spectroscopy confirms a 3.5‐fold higher recombination resistance in the p‐i‐n device, lowering recombination losses. Furthermore, this p‐i‐n architecture was validated in lead‐free FASnI 3 photodiodes, delivering a 135 dB LDR and a near‐infrared D* of 3.7 × 10 12 Jones. Finally, implementing these optimized devices in X‐ray detection systems yielded direct sensitivities of 2.0 and 1.77 µC Gyair − 1 cm − 2 for the triple‐cation and FASnI 3 configurations, respectively.
papers.filename: Humberto Emmanuel Sánchez‐Godoy, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, High-Performance Lead and Lead-Free Inverted Perovskite Photodiodes From Self-Powered Optical Sensing to X-Ray Detection

papers.titleEn: Efficient n-i-p all-perovskite tandem solar cells enabled by interconnection layer engineering
papers.abstract: All-perovskite tandem solar cells promise ultrahigh efficiencies, yet monolithic devices have been realized predominantly in the p–i–n architecture because n–i–p integration imposes stringent materials constraints. The preformed wide-bandgap top subcell and its hole-selective contact must withstand bottom-subcell fabrication temperatures, limiting material choices. Here we address this challenge using a 2.0 eV Cs-based all-inorganic wide-bandgap subcell and an additive-free P3HT hole-selective contact whose molecular organization is reconfigured by MeO-2PACz. This interfacial modification enhances P3HT ordering and promotes efficient hole extraction, alleviating a transport bottleneck in monolithic n–i–p tandems. Coupled with PCBM modification of the ALD-SnO₂ electron-selective contact in the 1.55 eV bottom subcell, this architecture enables balanced carrier coupling across the interconnection layer, suppresses charge accumulation and voltage loss, and delivers efficiencies of 25.3% and 24.7% for 0.096 cm² and 1.045 cm² devices, respectively, with a stabilized power output of 24.4%. Additionally, combining the n–i–p double-junction device with a p–i–n narrow-bandgap subcell (1.25 eV) yields a four-terminal triple-junction device with 28% efficiency. To our knowledge, this is the first report of an n–i–p double-junction device exceeding 25% efficiency and an n–i–p-based four-terminal triple-junction device reaching 28%, advancing perovskite tandem technology.
papers.filename: Jun Hong Noh, Nat. Commun., 2026, Efficient n-i-p all-perovskite tandem solar cells enabled by interconnection layer engineering

papers.titleEn: Molecular Engineered Hole Transport in Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells: A Comparative Study of Polymerized SAMs With Monomer SAMs and Polymeric HTLs
papers.abstract: Polymerized SAMs (self‐assembled molecules) emerge as compelling new hole transport materials for p‐i‐n perovskite solar cells. Structurally, they are a mixture of conventional monolayer SAMs and polymers, combining the best of both worlds by enabling homogeneous and scalable deposition with robustness toward solution concentration variations without compromising the charge transfer efficiency. This work systematically compares the polymerized SAMs Poly‐4PACz with the conventional monolayer SAMs MeO‐2PACz and Ph‐4PACz, as well as the polymer PTAA. Thorough X‐ray photon spectroscopy, contact angle, photoluminescence, and temperature‐dependent transient photocurrent measurements are presented, complemented with density functional theory calculations. All results considered, Poly‐4PACz’s key advantages include its solubility in the eco‐friendly solvent DMSO and its insensitivity to small variations in layer thickness, with excellent charge transport capabilities as deposited, making additional post‐deposition washing treatments obsolete. Furthermore, it possesses good wettability toward the perovskite solution and shows promising performance in both perovskite single‐junction (up to 19.4% PCE, 79% FF, 1.24V V oc ) and perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (up to 26.0% PCE, 78% FF, 1.92 V V oc ).

papers.titleEn: Direct Inkjet Printing of Covalent Organic Frameworks
authors: Louis C. P. M. de Smet
papers.corrAuthor: Louis C. P. M. de Smet
papers.abstract: There is a growing need for gas and volatile organic compound (VOC) sensors in many areas, including air quality, safety monitoring, and (early) disease detection. VOC sensors can make use of affinity coatings to increase their sensitivity and selectivity. With their intrinsic high surface areas and chemically tunable pores, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are excellent candidates for the design and fabrication of such affinity coatings. However, precise, scalable, and easy deposition of such COF materials is proven to still be a challenge. In this study, we show the controlled deposition of COFs through direct inkjet printing for the first time, for which COFs are prepared as colloidal suspensions, serving as ready-to-use inks. We present a facile colloidal synthesis, leading to colloidal suspensions that are stable for months and which allow inkjet printing without any further processing. The COFs can be printed on gold as both isolated spots and as thin layers. The synthesis and printing conditions were carefully optimized to strike the balance between colloidal stability, printing robustness, and controlled drying. After exposure to saturated VOC environments, the printed layers show VOC desorption as monitored by infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy, not only confirming partial retention of the porous nature of the printed COF particles but also demonstrating the applicability of printed COF layers as affinity coatings on VOC sensors.
papers.filename: Louis C. P. M. de Smet, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Direct Inkjet Printing of Covalent Organic Frameworks
